title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR just judgment = vindicative work; permission tip
pass_a_gloss: GAR: theologians say do not stop at natural propagation—lift minds to God's singular will, dispensation, and just judgment, meaning the vindicative work that inflicts punishment from vindicative justice (Scripture's judgment of God against men, Ezek. 11:9). Placeus's 'just judgment' here is only that nothing happens without God wisely and justly permitting. But in Rom. 2:5, 2 Thess. 1:5, Rev. 16:7 and 19:2 just judgment is not mere knowledge, wisdom, or permission—it designates judgment that inflicts penalties or distributes rewards by δικαιοκρισία, as Rev. 19:2 shows in condemning the great harlot who corrupted the earth. Tip before Placeus's Scripture-locution reply.
pass_b_english: GAR. For when the Theologians teach that one must not simply stick here in man's natural propagation, but that minds must be lifted higher to God's singular will and dispensation and his just judgment, what do we think they understand by the name of just judgment, if not that work of God by which he inflicts some punishment from the reason of vindicative justice—which Scripture calls the judgment of God against men, Ezek. 11:9? But what of the learned man? He acknowledges God's just judgment here because nothing is done, I know not whether with God unwilling, but with God wisely and justly permitting. Is that so? And does God's just judgment, when Scripture at Rom. 2:5, 2 Thess. 1:5, Rev. 16:7, 19:2 uses it, designate nothing but God's knowledge, wisdom, or permission? On the contrary, it designates God's judgment which either inflicts penalties according to desert or distributes rewards from the reason of that justice which is called δικαιοκρισία: as also in Rev. 19:2 God's just judgments are said to be constituted in this—that he condemned that great harlot who corrupted the earth with her fornication and avenged the blood of his servants from her hand.
source_text: GAR. Etenim cum docent Theologi, non esse hic simpliciter haerendum in naturali hominis propagatione, sed altius attollendos animos ad singularem voluntatem atque dispensationem Dei, & justum ipsius judicium, quid putamus justi judicii nomine ipsos intelligere; quam opus illud Dei, quo poenam aliquam ex ratione justitiae vindicatricis irrogat, quod Scriptura vocat judicium Dei contra homines Ezech. 11. 9. Quid autem vir doctus? Justum Dei judicium hic agnoscit, quia nihil fiat, nescio vel invito Deo, sed sapienter & juste permittente. Itane? Et justum judicium Dei cum Scriptura Rom. 2. 5. 2. Thess. 1. 5. Apoc. XVI. 7. XIX. 2. nihil aliud designat, quam cognitionem, sapientiam, aut permissionem Dei? Imo vero judicium Dei designat, quod vel poenas pro merito irrogat, vel praemia distribuit ex ratione justitiae illius, quae δικαιοκρισία dicitur: prout & Apoc. XIX. 2. justa Dei judicia in eo constituta dicuntur, quod meretricem illam magnam, quae corrupit terram scortatione sua, damnavit & vindicavit sanguinem servorum suorum ex manu eius.

choices.choice: Just judgment = vindicative work, not mere permission; Scripture cites
